ranked.headline: Computational methods assign cell identity across single-cell and spatial multi-omics
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell atlases now reach millions of cells, making annotation assessment without ground truth a practical need.

ranked.headline: Generative models conditioned on structural, epitope, or kinetic design targets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple generative peptide, antibody, and binder models to explicit conditioning targets across several biomolecular modalities.

ranked.headline: GPU acceleration and regulatory-block methods extend genomic association analysis
ranked.summary: Population-scale genomic datasets and GWAS workflows now demand scalable, interpretable tools for interaction, colocalisation, and variant-to-gene mapping.

ranked.headline: Standardized representations and programmatic access formalize reuse of biological data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints package curated data, policy-driven I/O and automated workflows as reusable infrastructure rather than standalone tools.

ranked.headline: Structural and k-mer variation links genomes to adaptation and trait prediction
ranked.summary: Chromosome-scale assemblies and population-scale variant maps now test adaptation and trait prediction in polyploid and non-model genomes.

ranked.headline: Benchmark confounds reshape how protein prediction models are evaluated
ranked.summary: Taxonomic and disorder confounds in protein benchmarks are prompting protocols that treat evaluation design as a primary result.

ranked.headline: Sequence models resolve specificity determinants in enzymes and peptide design
ranked.summary: Unsupervised fitness models and data-driven residue rankings now target altered specificity in enzymes and peptide design.

ranked.headline: Phylogenomic and k-mer tools address annotation and contamination in genomic data
ranked.summary: Recent tools pair protein language models and phylogenomic inference with decontamination and memory-efficient read classification.

ranked.headline: Workflow engines and GPU variant calling automate bioinformatics execution
ranked.summary: Three June 2026 preprints target runtime, orchestration, and GPU throughput in the execution layer of bioinformatics analysis.

ranked.headline: Sequence features track bacterial thermal adaptation and resistance gene evolution
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply genome-wide sequence, structure and population-scale analyses to bacterial adaptation and resistance evolution.

ranked.headline: Curvature-derived geometric encodings for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction
ranked.summary: June 2026 preprints add curvature-derived geometric inputs to protein-ligand affinity models, alongside a published drug-target affinity architecture.

ranked.headline: Learned models link molecular structure to property, toxicity, and antifungal readouts
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply graph, SMILES, and GAN-based models to ADMET, hERG, and hepatotoxicity endpoints.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks assess drug and perturbation response models on held-out and external data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test drug and perturbation response predictors on held-out, external, and zero-shot criteria rather than in-sample fit.

ranked.headline: Machine learning links pathogen genotypes and interactions to infectivity and virulence
ranked.summary: Pathogen phenotypes such as variant emergence, infectivity and virulence are now being predicted from sequence-derived, interaction-based and metabolic models.

ranked.headline: Anatomy-constrained models test how wiring and learning rules shape neural dynamics
ranked.summary: Measured connectomic, transcriptomic, and learning-rule constraints now serve as testable inductive biases for models of neural dynamics.

ranked.headline: Model structure and heterogeneity are tested against empirical snapshot and survey data
ranked.summary: Quantifying what observational data can constrain in mechanistic models now draws on flow cytometry snapshots, contact surveys, and outbreak case curves.

ranked.headline: Computational tools infer regulatory networks and TF binding across multi-omic datasets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers release R and Python tools for regulatory network inference, TF binding prediction, and integrative proteomics analysis.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools standardise ATAC, imaging and 3D morphometry feature extraction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints release open-source packages that standardise feature extraction and data formats across ATAC-seq, imaging, and transcriptomics.

ranked.headline: Cortical priors and neural decoders learn visual representations from diverse recordings
ranked.summary: Preprints now test whether cortical connectomes, single-cell spiking, and fMRI embeddings can yield transferable visual representations.

ranked.headline: Computational methods correct and model spatial and single-cell transcriptomic data
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics now demand computational corrections for artifacts and cross-species alignment before biological inference.

ranked.headline: Recombination and tree inference methods applied to viral and single-cell genomic data
ranked.summary: Viral sequence datasets and tree inference methods are being refined for artifact removal, recombination detection, and simulation.

ranked.headline: Plasma proteomics infers cell-type aging and archetypes linked to chronic disease risk
ranked.summary: Plasma proteomes now resolve aging at cell-type level and classify chronic disease risk across platforms, in cohorts of 11,900 to 60,542 people.

ranked.headline: Evidence-grounded LLM and graph models for biomedical prediction and question answering
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair LLM reasoning over structured biomedical evidence with held-out designs, ontology grounding, and contamination controls.

ranked.headline: LLM agents for bioinformatics: decomposing planning, recovery and interpretation
ranked.summary: Agentic bioinformatics pipelines are now being assessed per stage, with versioned skills and distilled tactics as checkable components.

ranked.headline: Machine learning models for omics anchored to reference labels or interpretable rules
ranked.summary: Machine learning on omics data is increasingly anchored to reference labels, donor-independent biomarkers, or sparse interpretable rules.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of genome structure and epigenome from sequencing reads
ranked.summary: Preprints and published studies now apply k-mer, foundation-model, and capture-based methods to sequencing data at finer resolution and greater sensitivity.

ranked.headline: Convergence does not ensure correct protein conformational ensembles
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and machine-learned models test whether simulated protein conformational ensembles are physically correct, not merely converged.

ranked.headline: Probabilistic factorization models encode sparsity and uncertainty in omics data
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs explicit priors and posterior inference with copy-number, factor-model, and multi-omics analysis.

ranked.headline: Calibration and auditing expose limits of biomedical ML model evaluation
ranked.summary: Biomedical ML studies increasingly test whether reported gains survive noise, calibration, localisation audits and data-sufficiency checks.

ranked.headline: Computational atomic modeling and validation of protein models against cryo-EM maps
ranked.summary: Limited-resolution and single-particle maps demand explicit geometric priors and real-time model-to-map checks.

ranked.headline: Computational tools for designing and modeling RNA and DNA sequence function
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple generative and scoring models to sequence-level objectives across RNA, DNA recombination, and mutagenesis library design.

ranked.headline: Agent-based and Bayesian simulations model cancer pathway faults and drug responses
ranked.summary: Mechanistic simulators now address multi-fault pathway behaviour, drug-combination ranking, and accelerated molecular dynamics forecasting.

ranked.headline: Auxiliary priors and covariates are encoded directly into biological network models
ranked.summary: Recent studies add external knowledge such as priors, covariates, and annotations to gene regulatory and protein complex network inference.

ranked.headline: Accelerated alignment and end-to-end workflows for sequencing and variant analysis
ranked.summary: Newly posted and published tools pair algorithmic speed-ups with standardized, end-to-end analysis workflows for sequencing and variant data.

ranked.headline: Learned models for RNA and protein design are now tested under explicit conditions
ranked.summary: Recent items apply learned predictors to siRNA efficacy, RNA structure, and Fanzor engineering, alongside RNA editing metrics, with defined evaluation contexts.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-mixed assembly from HiFi reads and GNN correction of De Bruijn graphs
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved assembly tools now target low-coverage and HiFi-only inputs, while primate diversity resources expand ploidy-aware variant data.

ranked.headline: Mechanical feedback and geometry shape stem cell and colony population outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple microscale mechanical and geometric rules to population-level outcomes in tissues, bacterial colonies, and mixed-cell migration fronts.

ranked.headline: Tractable models infer channel kinetics and oscillator phase dynamics from data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published OPC study pair mechanistic parameterization with tractable inference for neuronal and oscillatory dynamics.

ranked.headline: Learned models relate brain network connectivity to sex, stress and disease states
ranked.summary: Brain network models now link connectome, EEG and transcriptomic measures to sex, stress and Alzheimer's risk states.
